title: LiveNewsBench: Evaluating Web Search Agents with Freshly Curated News
claim: A fully automated two-stage pipeline turns fresh source documents into hard, verified question-answer pairs, illustrated by one example.
layout: 3 panels: two stacked left-to-right pipeline bands, plus a right example card
description: The figure has two horizontal rounded dashed bands on the left and a tall example card on the right. The top blue band, "1 News Article Acquisition", has four icon-and-caption steps linked by blue arrows: acquire news events from Wikipedia, search for relevant articles online, crawl and normalize from archive sites, and double-check relevance with LLMs. A large blue arrow labeled "News Articles" curves down into the bottom orange band, "2 Q&A Pair Creation". That band has four steps linked by orange arrows: draft multi-hop Q&A with an LLM, check answer correctness with self-consistency, check guideline adherence, and manual human review (green check and red X marks on people icons). An orange arrow leads to the right card, which shows a long multi-hop question about Guatemala's state of emergency in red, its answer in green, and the label "Human-Verified Test Set".
caption: Our automated dataset construction and one example from the Human-Verified Test Set. Our dataset construction pipeline comprises two main components: (1) retrieving news articles from online sources and (2) generating Q&A pairs from the retrieved content. Questions are designed to be challenging, requiring multiple searches, page visits, and reasoning steps.
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) with agentic web search capabilities show strong potential for tasks requiring real-time information access and complex fact retrieval, yet evaluating such systems remains challenging. We introduce LiveNewsBench, a rigorous and regularly updated benchmark designed to assess the agentic web search abilities of LLMs. LiveNewsBench automatically generates fresh question-answer pairs from recent news articles, ensuring that questions require information beyond an LLM's training data and enabling clear separation between internal knowledge and search capability. The benchmark features intentionally difficult questions requiring multi-hop search queries, page visits, and reasoning, making it well-suited for evaluating agentic search behavior. Our automated data curation and question generation pipeline enables frequent benchmark updates and supports construction of a large-scale training dataset for agentic web search models, addressing the scarcity of such data in the research community. To ensure reliable evaluation, we include a subset of human-verified samples in the test set. We evaluate a broad range of systems using LiveNewsBench, including commercial and open-weight LLMs as well as LLM-based web search APIs. The leaderboard, datasets, and code are publicly available at \url{livenewsbench.com}.
